In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–2} Allah the Exalted swears by the pen, a generic noun that includes all the pens with which kinds of knowledge are written and by which prose and poetry are inscribed. The pen and what it inscribes of various kinds of speech are among His great signs, which deserve that Allah swear by them to the innocence of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) from what his enemies attributed to him of madness. So He negated that from him by the blessing of his Lord upon him and His kindness to him, in that He bestowed upon him perfect intellect, sound judgment, and decisive speech, which is the finest of what pens have ever written and people have ever inscribed. This is happiness in this world.

{3} Then He mentioned his happiness in the Hereafter, saying: {And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off}; that is, a great reward, as the indefiniteness indicates, uninterrupted, rather constant and continuous. This is because of the righteous deeds, the complete character, and the guidance to every good that he (ﷺ) had sent forth before.

{4} For this reason He said: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}; that is, you are upon it, exalted by your character, which Allah has bestowed upon you. The sum of his great character is what his mother, the Mother of the Believers ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), explained when someone asked her about it; she said: "His character was the Qur'an." This is like the saying of the Exalted: {Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant} [7:199], {So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them…} [3:159], {There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer…} [9:128], and what is similar to these verses, which indicate his attribute of noble character (ﷺ), and the verses that urge every beautiful character. He had of them the most complete and most excellent, and in every one of these qualities he was at the highest summit. He (ﷺ) was easy and gentle, near to the people, responsive to the invitation of whoever invited him, fulfilling the need of whoever asked him, consoling the heart of whoever requested from him, not depriving him or sending him away disappointed. When his companions wished something from him, he agreed with them and followed them in it if there was no prohibition in it; and if he resolved upon a matter, he did not act arbitrarily without them, but consulted and sought their counsel. He accepted from their good-doers and pardoned their wrong-doers. He never associated with a companion except with the most complete and best companionship. He did not frown in his face, nor was harsh in his speech, nor withheld his cheerfulness from him, nor held against him the slips of his tongue, nor took him to account for any coarseness that came from him, but rather he was utmost in kindness to him and bore with him to the utmost degree of forbearance (ﷺ).

{5–6} When Allah had caused him to descend to the highest of stations in every respect, and his enemies were attributing to him that he was a madman possessed, He said: {So you will see and they will see. Which of you is the afflicted one?} It became clear that he was the most guided of people and the most perfect for himself and for others, and that his enemies were the most astray of people and the most harmful to people, and that they were the ones who tempted the servants of Allah and led them astray from His path. Allah's knowledge of that suffices, for He is the Reckoner and the Recompenser.

{7} {Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided}. In this there is a warning to the astray and a promise to the guided, and an explanation of the wisdom of Allah, in that He guides whoever is fit for guidance and not others.

They are not worthy of being obeyed, because they command only what agrees with their desires, and they want nothing but falsehood. Whoever obeys them moves toward what harms him. {10} ﴿And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾. That is, one who swears excessively. {11} ﴿A defamer, going about with slander﴾. That is, one who frequently finds fault with people and attacks them through backbiting, mockery, and other means. ﴿Going about with slander﴾ means he walks among people carrying tales, which is conveying one person's words to another with the intent of causing discord between them and stirring up enmity and hatred.

{12} ﴿A preventer of good﴾: one who withholds what he is obliged to give, such as obligatory expenditures, expiations, and zakat, and other such things. ﴿A transgressor﴾ against people, wronging them in their lives, their property, and their honor. ﴿Sinful﴾, that is, one who commits much sin and many wrongs concerning the right of God [Exalted].

{13} ﴿Brutal, and beyond that, of illegitimate birth﴾. That is, harsh and coarse in character, cruel, not submitting to the truth. ﴿Of illegitimate birth﴾ means a foundling with no true origin and no root from which good can grow; his character is of the worst kind, and no success is to be hoped from him. ﴿Of illegitimate birth﴾ also means he bears a mark of evil by which he is recognized.

{14} The sum of this is that God forbade obeying every habitual swearer, liar, base of soul, and wicked of character, especially those traits that involve self-admiration, arrogance toward the truth and toward creation, contempt for people through backbiting and slander, attacking them, and committing many sins.

{15} Although these verses were revealed concerning some of the polytheists, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or others, because of His saying about him: ﴿That he has wealth and sons. When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the former peoples"﴾. That is, because of the abundance of his wealth and children he became insolent and arrogant toward the truth, rejected it when it came to him, and counted it among the tales of the ancients, whose truth or falsehood can be debated. Yet the verses are general to everyone who possesses this attribute, because the Qur'an was revealed to guide all creation, and it includes the first and last of this Community. Sometimes a verse is revealed concerning a particular cause or a particular person, so that the general principle becomes clear through it, and through it the like of the particular instances that fall under general rulings become known.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 68, verses 17–33:**

{17–18} He, exalted is He, says: We tested these deniers of good, and We gave them respite, and We extended them with whatever We willed of wealth, children, long life, and the like, which accords with their desires. This is not because of any honour they have with Us. Rather, it may be an *istidraj* (a gradual leading-on) for them from where they do not know. Their being deceived by this is like the deception of the people of the garden, who were its partners, when its trees had ripened and its fruits had blossomed, and the time of its harvesting had come. They were certain that it was in their hands and at their command, and that there was no obstacle preventing them from it. For this reason they swore and made oaths, without saying "if God wills," that they would surely harvest it, that is, cut its fruit in the morning. They did not realise that God is ever watchful, and that the punishment would come upon them in it and hasten to them.

{19–20} ﴿Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord﴾, that is, a punishment descended upon it by night, ﴿while they were asleep﴾, so it destroyed it and ruined it. ﴿And it became like the darkness﴾, that is, like the dark night, and the trees and fruits were gone.

{21–22} This happened while they were unaware of this calamity. For this reason they called to one another when they awoke in the morning, saying to one another: ﴿Go early to your tilth, if you are going to harvest.﴾
